_comment: Scoring rules extracted from 01-San-Diego-Breaks/Central-SD.md and South-County.md (researched 2026-08-27). Degree windows are DERIVED from the compass directions in those write-ups, not from a degree-publishing source -- the folder is explicit that no public source publishes degree windows for these spots except Black's. Treat them as approximations of the prose.
_face_note: size_ideal / size_max are FACE feet, matching how the write-ups talk about size.
_board_swaps_note: board_ladder rungs are keyed on face height alone. Optional board_swaps override the rung when CONDITIONS, not size, decide the board: {face:[lo,hi], max_wind (mph), min_period (s), primary, backup, note}. First match wins; a swap never overrides a null 'don't paddle out' rung. Added 2026-08-29 for the mini-Simmons, whose limit is takeoff shape and surface texture rather than wave height -- see 02-Gear/Mini-Simmons-Deep-Dive.md. Board names here must match the nine in 02-Gear/Owned-and-Wishlist.md, same as the ladder. || CALIBRATION WARNING (added 2026-08-30 after external audit): the gate values (face <=5-5.5 ft, max_wind 8 mph, min_period 9-10 s) are PERSONAL HEURISTICS, not design facts -- no source validates those breakpoints. They are plausible and directionally sound, but they should be recalibrated from real session logs, and the better eventual design is a soft suitability read (face texture, entry steepness, power, wind, tide, rider confidence) rather than hard cutoffs. See 02-Gear/Mini-Simmons-Deep-Dive.md.

breaks.name: Black's Beach
breaks.dir_note: Optimum clean long-period WNW 280-290 deg -- the one spot with a published degree window
breaks.tide_note: Less tide-fussy the bigger it gets
breaks.skill: Intermediate to advanced, depending on size
breaks.hazards: CITY GUIDANCE: 'Access to Black's Beach is very difficult due to the high cliffs and unimproved and unmaintained trails. The SAFEST ACCESS IS FROM ADJACENT BEACHES TO THE NORTH AND SOUTH, but this access may be obstructed by high tides or surf. The cliffs are unstable and slides can occur without warning.' Check the tide before committing to a beach walk. Two significant rips, no designated swim zones. 72hr post-rain rule.
breaks.verdict: Best beachbreak in the county, and it's not close. The canyon doubles long-period swell here while it starves Scripps and the Shores -- same swell, different planet.
board_ladder: Small day -- the canyon's asleep and it's just another beachbreak
Chest-to-head with real push behind it
Big enough that paddle power starts winning arguments

GAP -- don't talk yourself into it. The Magic is a trim-and-glide board at ~37-39L, not a step-up, and the folder says plainly it is 'not the tool when the canyon is doubling a 16-second swell.' Locals: 'Blacks is all about late drops -- unless you are on a bigger board you will not be able to catch waves.' This is the Dredgernaut's job.

water.note: Standard county post-rain rule applies. No chronic source nearby.

breaks.name: Scripps Pier
breaks.dir_note: WNW. Rights dominate. South swell is the worst case -- canyon shadow to -64%
breaks.tide_note: Mid on a rising push -- fussiest of the three canyon spots
breaks.hazards: Permitted outfalls in the area, including SIO's monitored filtered-seawater discharge and stormwater south of the pier -- treat as runoff-adjacent after rain rather than a chronically polluting drain. 72hr post-storm rule. Pier is UCSD property, closed to the public.
breaks.verdict: Size-starved far more often than maxed -- '79% too small' in January. The canyon shadow, doing what it does.
board_ladder: Egg water -- ~40-43L of float for a shadowed little day
It reads '79% too small' for a reason -- reach for the fish before the Rosa most days
Chest-to-head with push -- the Rosa's home break, F8 Legacy Large in it

board_swaps.note: Same shadow as the Shores, same soft rolling takeoff -- clean and lined up, this is Simmons water well past waist-high. Not a grovel, a glide.

water.note: Runoff-adjacent: permitted outfalls nearby, stormwater south of the pier. County post-rain rule applies with the outlet caveat. Earlier wording ('polluting drain directly at the beach') was an overstatement, corrected 2026-08-30.

breaks.name: La Jolla Shores
breaks.dir_note: W best, NW works. Rights dominate
breaks.tide_note: Breaks on whatever tide you show up to
breaks.hazards: Stingrays are the signature hazard -- do the shuffle. Rips and undertow. Checkered flag zones swim from surf.
breaks.verdict: The overflow lot. Deepest canyon shadow of the three (-40% to -89%) and long period actually hurts it. But when a south wind ruins everywhere else, this place shrugs.
board_ladder: Genuinely tiny -- exactly what you own the glider for
Soft, shadowed, gutless -- and the Simmons turns gutless into speed. Panther if you'd rather walk; the Greenough 4-A finally gets to do its thing
North end toward Scripps carries noticeably more punch than the south

board_swaps.note: Clean past waist-high is the Simmons' actual wheelhouse -- softest takeoff of the bunch, so it gets the widest band. Draw long lines and trim high; it doesn't do vertical and doesn't want to.

breaks.name: PB Point
breaks.dir_note: NW and W only -- unanimous across sources
breaks.tide_note: Low to mid. Fattens up and goes soft on the high
breaks.hazards: Documented localism: do not park up by the cliff on a good swell (wax on windshields). Stay away from the hut area halfway down the point. Reef at the top is protected by the shortboarding crew.
breaks.verdict: Flat when PB's fun, working when PB's blown. Needs a real swell just to show up -- 3-5ft before it's a wave at all.
board_ladder: Below turn-on size -- but if it's breaking at all, bigger boards rule the peak

About as close to purpose-built for the Magic as SD gets -- 'it's the slowest wave around' and 'bigger boards rule.' Frye 7.5" for hold through the long sections; drop to the 6.5" if it feels stiff. Big winter days are the Dredgernaut's, once it exists

breaks.name: Crystal Pier
breaks.dir_note: Widest window of the group -- N, NW, W, SW
breaks.tide_note: Mid to high. The rising-vs-falling argument is unsettled -- sources split
breaks.hazards: Pier pilings and rips near them. The most contested lineup in PB -- surfers bunch at the wedge off the pier. Parking is notoriously hard.
breaks.verdict: The dependable one in PB. Sit a little north of the pier and let everyone else fistfight over the wedge.
board_ladder: Fish gets the nod -- catches more of the small stuff, and you skip the scrum at the one good peak

breaks.name: PB Drive
breaks.dir_note: Reportedly works on any direction; PB-wide answer is W/NW/SW
breaks.tide_note: Mid to high, but the sandbars move and take the answer with them
breaks.hazards: Rips. Little else -- this is the mellowest lineup of the ten.
breaks.verdict: Mellowest lineup on the list, peaks spread everywhere. Fall combo swells are its whole personality. Walls up and shuts down once it's overhead on long period.
board_ladder: The local book says 'fish or funboard,' and the local book is right
'Fish or funboard, especially during those Autumn combo swells'

board_swaps.note: Clean, lined-up sandbar rights are a down-the-line planing wave -- the Simmons outruns the fish here when there's real period underneath. 10s minimum: this stretch wants swell, not slop.

breaks.name: Mission Beach
breaks.dir_note: NW and SW. Crossed-up combo swell is what makes it good
breaks.tide_note: Mid. Low tide plus size equals closeouts
breaks.hazards: Strong rips -- stay ~100m off the South Jetty. Rose and Tecolote Creeks exceed state recreation standards at least half the time even in dry weather.
breaks.verdict: Reliably average. The good version needs everything at once: crossed-up combo swell, a bank that showed up, offshore E before 11am, moderate size. A big clean long-period swell straight at it is the worst case -- one long closeout.
board_ladder: The two things that fix this spot aren't boards: walk further than everyone else, and be in before 11am
Rosa on a proper combo day, fish the rest of the time

board_swaps.note: Clean chest-high Mission is a genuinely fun Simmons day. Capped at 4.5ft because this beach walls and shuts down at size -- and a flat-rockered nose has no exit from a closeout.

water.note: Mission Bay's Rose and Tecolote Creeks exceed state recreation standards at least half the time EVEN IN DRY WEATHER. Stay clear of the south jetty and the bay side.
water.outlet: Rose and Tecolote Creeks into Mission Bay

breaks.name: OB Pier
breaks.dir_note: W, NW, SW, SSW -- 'a swell with a little W in the mix'
breaks.tide_note: Low to mid, but honestly breaks on whatever -- least tide-fussy of the OB spots
breaks.hazards: PIER CLOSED since Oct 2023, a support pile broke off into the ocean Dec 2023 -- broken pile in the water, demolition from 2027. Swim-only zone between the pier and Dog Beach is ticketable. Water 'toxic if the San Diego River is flowing.'
breaks.verdict: Surfline's words: 'temperamental, shifty, unpredictable, perennially surfed and most often mediocre.' Check it on the way to somewhere else.
board_ladder: Mediocre, crowded, close to home, zero stakes -- the Waterhog's entire reason to exist
Fish or Rosa on paper. Waterhog in practice, more days than not

board_swaps.note: Low-stakes sand on a clean morning -- the right classroom for learning what the Simmons does past waist-high. The water, not the wave, is the catch here.

water.note: 'Fair -- not great most days and TOXIC IF THE SAN DIEGO RIVER IS FLOWING.'
water.outlet: San Diego River mouth just north

breaks.name: OB Jetty
breaks.tide_note: Mid to low, breaks on most tides
breaks.wind_note: No kelp here, so unlike Sunset Cliffs it won't tolerate onshore NW
breaks.skill: Advanced -- 'not the place to go unless you are confident in your abilities'
breaks.hazards: WORST WATER QUALITY OF THE TEN. Breaks directly in front of Dog Beach at the river outlet. A County advisory ran from April 2, 2026. Check sdbeachinfo.com or 619-338-2073 before paddling out -- every time. Localism flagged as a hazard.
breaks.verdict: A sandbar with moods -- good years and bad ones. Steep little takeoff into a fast right wall; Surfline rates the jetty right the best wave around here.
board_ladder: Below its range -- the bank needs size to do its thing. Advanced-only spot; not a Waterhog day.
Steep takeoff into a fast wall -- thruster surfing, not trim. Only when the bank's good

water.note: WORST WATER QUALITY OF THE TEN. Breaks directly in front of Dog Beach at the river outlet. A County advisory ran from April 2, 2026 -- a spring, NON-STORM advisory. The river falls out here year-round. Check sdbeachinfo.com or 619-338-2073 every single time.

breaks.name: Sunset Cliffs
breaks.dir_note: W, NW, SW. Ideal angle from the west paired with an east offshore
breaks.tide_note: Low to mid and specifically RISING -- two independent sources call that out. Mid to high can go slow to nonexistent
breaks.hazards: MOST DANGEROUS SPOT IN THE GUIDE. An average of 5 deaths or serious injuries per year, 2005-2018. The cliffs themselves are the danger -- people have been battered against them trying to exit. Active erosion, a bluff section broke off April 2026. Rope and peg descents are the norm. The tide governs your exit, not just the wave: surfers unfamiliar with the area are often unable to get back up the trails on bigger days at higher tides. Urchins, rips, rocks.
breaks.verdict: The kelp out the back irons out NW windbump -- when the afternoon onshore has wrecked PB, Mission and OB, the Cliffs are still combed. Most of these reefs don't properly wake up until it's overhead.
board_ladder: Under the reefs' wake-up size -- they 'only really start to work when it's overhead.' Garbage is the summer exception
Sub or Ab. Rock bottom, rope descents, cliff exits -- boards get dinged here, bring the right one anyway
Clean and well-overhead at Garbage or New Break -- long rights made for trim, and the Frye holds a line through those 300m walls. Run the 7.5"
NOTHING. Genuinely big at the outer reefs is not a day you own a board for. Wait for the step-up.

water.note: Best water quality of the ten -- away from the river mouth. 'Typically ok but gets dicey after a rain.'

breaks.name: Cardiff Reef
breaks.dir_note: W to WNW best; usable SW-W-NW
breaks.tide_note: Works all tides -- low to mid gives the better sections
breaks.hazards: Rocks. Otherwise the most forgiving reef in the guide -- no cliff exit, no rope descent, no urchin field.
breaks.verdict: The other kelp spot, and the reason it made the list first: a big bed plus wind-blocking cliffs keep it combed when the county's gone crumbly. Rated very consistent. Blown-out afternoon? This is the call before the Cliffs.
board_ladder: Slow, mushy, flat-bottomed reef -- honest glider water
Long soft walls, no push. Log it
The Magic's job description -- trim and glide down a long mushy wall. Frye 7.5" for hold
Bigger winter swell at low tide, when the south peak finally puts its shoulders into it

water.note: San Elijo Lagoon drains into the surf zone here. The County advisory explicitly names LAGOON OUTLETS as needing extra caution, so this is now a supported coastal-outlet classification, not an inference. Avoid after heavy rain.

breaks.name: Swami's
breaks.dir_note: W ideal, W/NW the money direction. Right point/reef over rock ledge
breaks.tide_note: Low to mid. Not a high-tide wave
breaks.skill: Intermediate at size; advanced once overhead
breaks.hazards: Rocks. Long stairway from the bluff-top lot. Lineup runs on informal rotation etiquette and dropping in is the cardinal sin -- tight-knit, but no documented aggression record.
breaks.verdict: Highest-rated wave in the research (4/5, '52% clean' in January) and the county's real answer once it's big. Holds to triple-overhead -- long after the quiver taps out.
board_ladder: One of the best longboard rights between SD and LA. Glide it
The Rosa's window -- and the stretch where Swami's extends your ceiling past anything in Central SD

CEILING -- above roughly head-and-a-half this is step-up / gun territory (sources say 8'0-9'0 for double-overhead and up). A 34.29L 6'0 is not that board. The block sits higher than Black's because a point takeoff is more forgiving than a Black's late drop, not because the quiver improved. Second spot after Black's and the Cliffs arguing for the Dredgernaut.

water.note: Standard county post-rain rule applies. No chronic source nearby.

breaks.name: Oceanside Pier
breaks.hidden_note: Hidden 2026-08-30: 49 min is too far for a daily call (Jake). Research and scoring rules kept -- flip hidden to false to restore, e.g. for a North County day or a trip stopover.
breaks.dir_note: Picks up swell from essentially every direction -- widest window in the guide. WSW groundswell ideal; NW wraps into the bay to feed rights
breaks.wind_note: Handles wind from any direction better than any Central beachbreak; NE offshore still cleans it up best. Blows out midday like everywhere else.
breaks.skill: All levels on the north side
breaks.hazards: NORTH SIDE ONLY. The south side is documented as a much more aggressive crowd -- locals 'not afraid to regulate their spot' -- and is shallower, hollower and heavier. Paid parking at the pier is very limited; street park and walk. Wisconsin St entry has occasional big rocks.
breaks.verdict: Very consistent, all tides, holds overhead, and November is its best clean month -- off-cycle from the January-dominant rest of the county. NOTE: an earlier claim that a submarine canyon amplifies swell into the pier was REMOVED 2026-08-30 as unsupported; Oceanside Canyon sits much farther offshore and there is no evidence of a Black's-class nearshore lens here.
board_ladder: Sand-bottom peaks, no consequence -- the fish catches more of them
Once it's got some push behind it
The bigger sandbar peaks. Sand bottom and a forgiving takeoff, which is why this doesn't block the way Black's does -- but it is past what the quiver is built for

water.note: San Luis Rey River mouth is roughly a mile north at the harbour. INFERENCE, not a documented advisory -- modestly extended post-rain window on that basis.
water.outlet: San Luis Rey River mouth ~1 mi north

_water_note: Water-risk profiles derived from the hazard sections of 01-San-Diego-Breaks/. The brief CANNOT read live County advisories. California publishes a machine-readable postings/closures dataset, but checked 2026-08-30 it was ~6 months stale and missing the then-active Imperial Beach and Coronado closures -- historical archive only, never a live gate. sdbeachinfo.com / 619-338-2073 remains authoritative. outlet_proximity (at|nearby|none) replaced invented rain_factor multipliers 2026-08-30, grounded in the County's own naming of storm drains, creeks, rivers and lagoon outlets.
_drive_note: drive_minutes / drive_miles are OSRM free-flow driving times from Jake's home neighbourhood (Mission Hills). Deliberately neighbourhood-level, not an address: THIS REPO IS PUBLIC. Free-flow is a fair approximation for the dawn window; the evening window sees real traffic, so treat the North County numbers as a floor. Breaks over DRIVE_FLAG_MINUTES (45) get a 'worth the drive?' marker -- scoring is NOT affected, per Jake's call 2026-08-30. Recomputed 2026-08-30 when Jake gave his location; the earlier numbers assumed Pacific Beach and were wrong for the PB and OB spots especially.
_north_county_note: Cardiff Reef, Swami's and Oceanside Pier added 2026-08-30 to close measured gaps (wind, high tide, size, crowd) rather than by reputation -- see 01-San-Diego-Breaks/North-County.md. Imperial Beach, the Tijuana Sloughs, Coronado and Windansea are deliberate exclusions, documented in the same file.
